images.filename: Gezicht op Maastricht (A F vd Meulen, 1673), detail 2.jpg
images.caption: Detail of a view of Maastricht, the Netherlands, from Mount Saint Peter, in 1673. The Brussels painter Adam Frans van der Meulen followed in the train of the French troops during the Siege of Maastricht by Louis XIV. He used this sketch for his paintings of this famous siege. Here the western ramparts and the church towers of St. Servatius' and St. John's.
images.alt: Detail of a view of Maastricht, the Netherlands, from Mount Saint Peter, in 1673. The Brussels painter Adam Frans van der Meulen followed in the train of the French troops during the Siege of Maastricht by Louis XIV. He used this sketch for his paintings of this famous siege. Here the western ramparts and the church towers of St. Servatius' and St. John's.

images.filename: Gezicht op Maastricht (A F vd Meulen, 1673), detail 1.jpg
images.caption: Detail of a view of Maastricht, the Netherlands, from Mount Saint Peter, in 1673. The Brussels painter Adam Frans van der Meulen followed in the train of the French troops during the Siege of Maastricht by Louis XIV and used this sketch for his paintings of this famous siege. In the centre Sint-Pieterspoort and the churches of St. Nicolas, Our Lady's and the Minorites. To the right: the Meuse bridge and Wyck. In the foreground: the village of Sint Pieter.
images.alt: Detail of a view of Maastricht, the Netherlands, from Mount Saint Peter, in 1673. images.caption: Maastricht, the Netherlands. View towards the East of Plein 1992, the main square of the Céramique neighbourhood on the East bank of the river Meuse, named after the Treaty of Maastricht (1992). The square was designed in the late 1990s by Dutch architect Jo Coenen, as well as several buildings around it, including the Centre Céramique library on the right. To the left: part of La Résidence by Swiss architect Aurelio Galfetti and French architect Yann Keromnes. At the far end: a fragment of La Fortezza by Mario Botta.
